back: A total well-being in all aspects of reproduction — physical, emotional, behavioural and social.
Reproductive and Child Health Care programmes — the improved programmes now in operation, covering wider reproduction-related areas than the family planning programmes started in 1951.

Some amniotic fluid of the developing foetus is taken to analyse foetal cells and dissolved substances; used to test for genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia and sickle-cell anaemia, and to determine foetal survivability.

front: Reason for banning amniocentesis for sex determination
back: To legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides. A female foetus is frequently followed by MTP, which is against the law.
A non-steroidal oral contraceptive developed at CDRI, Lucknow. It is a once-a-week pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

front: Periodic abstinence and the fertile period
back: Couples abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle, when ovulation is expected. This window is called the fertile period because chances of fertilisation are very high.
The male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination.

Absence of menstruation during intense lactation after parturition; ovulation and the cycle do not occur, so conception is almost impossible as long as the mother breast-feeds fully. Effective only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.

A thin rubber/latex sheath covering the penis (male) or the vagina and cervix (female) just before coitus, so ejaculated semen does not enter the female reproductive tract. Disposable and self-inserting; also protects against STIs and AIDS.

Reusable rubber barriers inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus, blocking the entry of sperms. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are used along with them to raise efficiency.
Non-medicated (Lippes loop), copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20).

They increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus; copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. Hormone-releasing IUDs additionally make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

One pill daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle, then a 7-day gap during which menstruation occurs; the pattern repeats till conception is to be prevented.
They inhibit ovulation and implantation, and alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard the entry of sperms.
Progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs administered within 72 hours of coitus; used after rape or casual unprotected intercourse.
Male sterilisation: a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum. Blocks gamete transport; highly effective but poorly reversible.
Female sterilisation: a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina. Highly effective but poorly reversible.
User-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible, with no or the least side-effects, and no interference with sexual drive, desire or the sexual act.
Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term. About 45-50 million MTPs are performed worldwide in a year, roughly one-fifth of all conceived pregnancies.

Termination within the first 12 weeks on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner; between 12 and 24 weeks, on the opinion of two practitioners formed in good faith that a required ground exists.

front: Grounds for MTP under the 2017 Act
back: (i) Continuation of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to physical or mental health; (ii) substantial risk that the child, if born, would suffer physical or mental abnormalities making it seriously handicapped.
Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV leading to AIDS. HIV infection is the most dangerous.

front: Which STIs are not completely curable
back: Hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection. All other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
Pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, and even cancer of the reproductive tract.
Inability to produce children in spite of unprotected sexual co-habitation — inability to conceive even after 2 years of unprotected cohabitation.

front: IVF followed by ET (test tube baby programme)
back: Ova from the wife/donor and sperms from the husband/donor are collected and induced to form a zygote under simulated laboratory conditions; the zygote or early embryo is then transferred to complete development.

ZIFT (zygote intra fallopian transfer) places a zygote or early embryo of up to 8 blastomeres in the fallopian tube. IUT (intra uterine transfer) places an embryo of more than 8 blastomeres in the uterus.

Gamete intra fallopian transfer — an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and development.
Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection — a sperm is directly injected into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory.
Semen collected from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI). Used where the male cannot inseminate the female or has very low sperm counts.

front: Population figures quoted in the chapter
back: World: 2 billion in 1900, about 6 billion by 2000, 7.2 billion in 2011. India: about 350 million in 1947, close to 1 billion by 2000, crossing 1.2 billion in May 2011.
Less than 2 per cent, i.e., 20 per 1000 per year. Brought down only marginally through the RCH programme, so serious measures were needed to check it.
